label: chairs or heads organization
definition: The first person holds or held the chair or head leadership office of the second organization or committee.
scope_notes: Chairman/chair and head/lead together dominate the full dictionary. This is an office relationship, not generic membership: member/serve-on/sit-on form a substantial competing family. Historical offices count. Generic political descriptions require a resolved individual; chairmanship of a panel owned by a larger body does not alone establish chairmanship of that larger body.

facts.reason: Tyson is explicitly chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers.
Rohatyn is directly chairman of and heads Municipal Assistance Corporation, including an explicit as-chairman construction.
This is an organization receiving the Nobel Peace Prize, not a person heading an organization. The truncated first name cannot turn award receipt into chairmanship.
Bradford serves on and is a member of the NRC. The relative clause connects membership to the NRC; the separate chairman apposition does not say he chairs this commission.

Several paths explicitly describe chairing or heading the Senate Armed Services Committee, but the first argument is only Democrat. The extraction does not identify which individual this latent entity denotes; membership and panel-level evidence are also mixed in.
facts.reviewer_question: Which named Democrat is the first argument, and do these committee-chair references all denote that individual?
